messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: PagerDuty fired for service=canary-embed-checks severity=critical incident=inc_1768881234
maya: acked and on the bridge. seeing a large spike in 5xxs for /v1/embed since the canary rolled out ~25m ago
kevin: ack. I'm pulling traces and logs now. assigning to kevin/sre to dig in.
pd-bot: PagerDuty incident inc_1768881234 acknowledged by maya
maya: quick context: release 2026-03-14/9b1d4c rolled a canary at ~5% traffic, toggled autobatching=true for the canary variant
alex: joining bridge (zoom: https://zoom.company/bridge-1768881234). linking to tracing + rollout console
kevin: initial trace sample shows upstream timeouts from model-proxy and repeated kv-cache misses on worker side, leads to retries and 502s
kevin: sample log snippet:
```
2026-03-14T21:14:02Z model-proxy ERROR req=ef12 path=/v1/embed status=502 err="upstream timeout after 10s"
2026-03-14T21:14:02Z kv-cache INFO key=kv://ac3d miss
```
samir: any other config changes besides autobatching? batching window? retry policy?
maya: no other changes in canary besides enabling autobatching to improve throughput/cost
kevin: repro locally with canary config: autobatching increases concurrent inflight requests, which seems to cause kv-cache saturation on model worker nodes -> longer RPC tails -> 502s back at proxy
maya: proposed quick mitigations: (A) reduce canary traffic to ~0.5% (B) disable autobatching on canary replicas as a hotfix
alex: executing traffic adjustment via rollout manager now
ops-bot: Command executed: `redwoodctl traffic set --service canary-embed-checks --percent 0.5 --reason "mitigate 5xx"`
ops-bot: Response: accepted, canary traffic now 0.5%
kevin: preparing k8s patch to flip AUTOBATCH env var to false on canary pods
kevin: kubectl patch command:
```
kubectl -n inference patch deployment canary-embed-checks --type=json -p='[{"op":"replace","path":"/spec/template/spec/containers/0/env/0/value","value":"false"}]'
```
maya: applying patch and watching rolling restart
incident-bot: Escalation policy triggered -> SEV2 rotation notified
oncall-rotation: primary oncall has acknowledged, escalating to secondary (samir)
samir: here. verifying region breakdowns. eu-west looks recovered after traffic shift; us-west still elevated
kevin: on the node level we see kv-cache capacity warnings on nodes worker-21, worker-22; patch will restart pods and clear the transient pressure faster than bumping cache config which requires full build
alex: if errors don't trend down in 5 minutes we should plan a rollback to previous revision. rollback runbook ready
maya: monitoring: 90s after patch, 5xx rate on /v1/embed dropped from ~5.2% -> 1.1%
kevin: worker metrics show kv hit-rate recovering and retry queue lengths decreasing
alex: customer impact estimate: approximate 0.7% of total embedding requests got 5xxs between 21:10-21:16; early reports appearing in status page
maya: created internal incident ticket: https://incidents.company/inc_1768881234 with summary and initial impact
pd-bot: Auto-escalation suppressed because incident acknowledged
ops-bot: Rollback command if needed: `redwoodctl rollout undo --service canary-embed-checks --to-revision previous`
kevin: no further 502 spikes after patch, trending to baseline. continuing to watch for 30m before full canary ramp
samir: please add a runbook entry: autobatching on canary can increase kv-cache pressure; suggest a preflight load test for autobatch toggles
maya: drafting status page message: "Investigating elevated error rate on embeddings endpoint; mitigation in progress" and will update with timeframe once stable
alex: note: nginx layer did not show 504s; root cause appears proxy->worker path with cache pressure
maya: p99 error rate back at baseline (<0.1%) at 21:28; canary traffic held at 0.5% until we confirm stability
kevin: action items for postmortem: [1] add per-replica kv-cache capacity alerting, [2] update canary runbook about autobatching risk, [3] add stress test for autobatching with reduced kv cache
maya: postmortem owner assigned: kevin. draft due by EOD
samir: oncall will monitor for the next 30m, escalate if regressions occur
alex: handing off bridge watch to oncall-rotation. I'll stay available for 10 more minutes
oncall-rotation: acknowledged. taking over monitoring duties
incident-bot: Incident inc_1768881234 status -> resolved by maya at 2026-03-14T21:34: - closing after stability period
maya: closing thread. thanks all for quick coord. :white_check_mark:
